items.title: National Grid launches North West London Upgrade project to strengthen electricity network and support future growth
items.summary: National Grid has launched its North West London Upgrade (NWLU) project, a major investment designed to strengthen the electricity transmission network, support future growth and unlock new connections across North West London and surrounding areas.Spanning from Sundon substation in Bedfordshire to Elstree substation in Hertfordshire, and on to St John’s Wood substation in London, the complex programme includes new and upgraded substations, new cables, and reinforcement of existing overhead lines.

items.title: Budding young scientists in Rowde inspired by National Grid’s latest STEM session
items.summary: Using energy sticks that lit up when a circuit was complete, the children carried out a range of experiments to discover which everyday materials allow electricity to flow and which stop it in its tracks. Many of the children were surprised to learn that they could conduct electricity themselves by joining hands to create human circuits that lit up the energy sticks.

items.title: National Grid Introduces New Customer Protections During Periods of Extreme Heat
items.summary: The company will pause service disconnections for nonpayment for residential electric customers on any day when the heat index is forecast to be 90 degrees or higher. Disconnection is the absolute last resort for National Grid and only occurs after company representatives have attempted to assist customers to eliminate any overdue balances. The company has a suite of programs to aid customers that have fallen behind on their bills and communicates frequently with customers who miss a payment deadline or have overdue balances.

items.title: National Grid Seeks to Freeze Gas Delivery Rates for Customers in New York City and on Long Island
items.summary: National Grid today filed a Rate Stabilization Proposal with the New York State Public Service Commission (PSC) to freeze gas delivery rates for the company’s 1.9 million customers in New York City and on Long Island. If approved, rates for gas customers approved under the current rate plan would remain in effect for one additional year, from April 1, 2027, to March 31, 2028.
